meta.title: Frondia — what actually changed
meta.description: An evidence atlas of five Belgian cities, Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent, Liège and Charleroi: what each sector lacks, what to place where, and what actually changed in its green, against a noise threshold measured on the city itself.

hero.title: What actually changed.
hero.lede: Every summer the city’s green rustles — and so does every new edition of its map. Frondia tells the rustle from the growth.
hero.caption: An illustration, not a measurement.

proof.title: The map changed. The trees, far less.
proof.body: A new edition of a map can move more than a city does. Before reading any change, Frondia asks what moved: the ground, or the way it was drawn.

Read as change, the official map says each of the {count} cities gained {min} to {max} points of canopy. Over the sectors of Antwerp and Ghent the aerial photographs cover, it gained {oa} and {og}; the aerial photographs, {pa} and {pg}.

region.close: Across the region the same map reads {s21} in {a} and {s23} in {b}. Against twelve matched places, {loss} sectors lose beyond noise and {gain} gain; the strongest loss is the one pictured. The rest is a shift across the whole city. Bruxelles Environnement names continuing urbanisation as the main cause, and better mapping as a lesser one.

law.title: Since 2024, Europe counts urban green by law.
law.p1: Article 8 of the Nature Restoration Regulation: no net loss of urban green space and tree canopy from 2024 to 2030, then an upward trend, monitored with Copernicus. Belgium missed the 1 September 2026 deadline for its national restoration plan: the Brussels and Walloon parts were not ready.
law.p2: Cities where green already exceeds 45% and canopy 10% are exempt. Computed with the Commission’s own method, by municipality:
law.communes: Find your commune: its test, its hectares, what changed since 2024
law.close: Official layers say how much. Frondia says whether it changed beyond noise, and why. By rank the two agree: the official canopy layer and the three canopy instruments Frondia uses correlate at r = {lo}–{hi} across the {count} cities.

audiences.text: Whether green space and canopy grew or shrank after the 2024 baseline, sector by sector, with the noise measured and every loss named. Bruxelles Environnement in Brussels; in Flanders, ANB and INBO, which runs the monitoring; in Wallonia, the SPW.
audiences.cta: See the cities in the atlas

audiences.text: Which sectors lack services, shops within reach, shade or a bench; where the next objects should go; and whether a new park changed the ground, summer after summer.
A check written into the grant before the works start. The outline, the baseline and the comparison places are fixed with a date, so nobody can draw the result to fit afterwards.

threshold.title: The threshold is measured, not chosen.
steps: Every sector of the city takes one turn as a pretend intervention.
It is matched to twelve sectors that had the same greenness and summer heat beforehand and lie far enough away not to share its building sites.
Its “effect” is recorded. Nothing happened there, so the spread of all {n} effects is the method’s own noise. The city threshold is where 95% of it ends: ±{thr} in {city}.

three.title: What’s missing
three.text: Everyday services for a family, from a school to a tram stop: the worst-served fifth of the city is the darkest. The same lens shows shops within reach, summer heat and the 3-30-300 rule.

three.title: What to place
three.text: Where the next public toilets should go, ranked by the demand each one would cover. Ten points of each of fourteen kinds of object were named in September 2026, before anyone placed anything.

three.title: What changed
three.text: Greener or browner beyond the city’s own noise, against twelve places that looked the same beforehand. Only this step is a measurement of change; the other two describe and recommend.

audits.title: Three places measured beyond noise, each with its caveat printed.
audits.p1: An audit measures the footprint of the works itself against twelve sectors named in the atlas, then follows the effect summer by summer, because a park that greened once and faded is a different story.
audits.p2: Its threshold is calibrated for the audit’s own instrument and years, so it differs from the city threshold above. Drag or tap a picture to compare before and after.

audits.altAfter: {place} after the works, Sentinel-2 summer composite {window}
audits.compare: Compare {place} before and after the works
audits.noImage: No before/after picture: at 30 m a {ha}-hectare park is about fifteen pixels across. The series below is the evidence.
audits.open: Open the audit in the atlas

ninove.title: A wasteland by the canal became a meadow park.
ninove.story: Parc de la Porte de Ninove opened in autumn 2019 on a vacant lot where Anderlecht, Molenbeek and the City of Brussels meet.
ninove.reading: Sealed ground went down and grass went up, and a second instrument agrees. Canopy did not pass its own threshold: this is a meadow park, and the verdict says so.

droogdokkenpark.title: +0.29 on paper. Half of it was a building site.
droogdokkenpark.story: The Belvédère opened in September 2018 on the old dry docks of Eilandje. The standard “before” window caught the works in progress.
droogdokkenpark.reading: With a baseline taken before the works, the defensible effect is half the headline and still three times the threshold. That baseline rests on the two usable scenes of summer 2016.
droogdokkenpark.imageNote: The “before” picture is the standard 2017–19 window, when the works were already under way. The number above uses the 2016 baseline instead.

spoor-noord.title: A rail yard became nineteen hectares of grass.
spoor-noord.story: The NMBS marshalling yard opened as a park in 2008–2009. Sentinel-2 did not exist yet, so the audit uses Landsat, which reaches back to 2006.
spoor-noord.reading: The one summer in the noise is the 2018 drought, when a grass park loses its lead over everything around it. There is no second instrument for these years.

refuse.title: A tool that answers everything with a number is useless. This one says where it stops.
refuse.body: Each rule below was added after a convincing, wrong result showed up without it. The counts are how often each one fired on real data.

refusals.head: Cooling
refusals.text: Our noise floor for surface temperature is larger than what a new park realistically does to it. So nowhere on this site does a park “cool the street by a degree”.

refusals.head: Places with no fair comparison
refusals.text: A park at the edge of the scale has nothing similar to be compared with. When the matched places differ too much beforehand, Frondia refuses the verdict.

refusals.head: One-season alarms
refusals.text: A single brown summer is weather more often than loss. A drop is published only when a second, independent instrument sees the canopy go and no construction appear.

refusals.head: Restorations
refusals.text: Fixing paths, ponds and fountains in a park that is already green does not show from space. Older park projects, seven large restorations among them, each measured with its own window and threshold, sit within the noise.

refusals.head: Causes without documents
refusals.text: The strongest greening in Brussels, Zavelenberg, is a nature reserve where grazing stopped after the farmer died. Without a document, no cause is named.

faq.a: No. The atlas also shows what each sector lacks, from everyday services and shops within reach to summer heat and the 3-30-300 rule, and where the next of fourteen kinds of public object should go. Only greenness is measured as change against the city’s own noise; the rest are states and recommendations, and the atlas labels them that way.

faq.q: Does it measure trees, or just “green”?
faq.a: The main instrument is greenness: the vegetation index from Sentinel-2. A second one, Dynamic World, tells trees, grass and sealed ground apart, and a loss of canopy is published only when both agree. By rank, Frondia’s canopy and the official and independent canopy layers agree at {canopyR}.

faq.q: Who draws the outline of a project? Could it be drawn to fit the result?
faq.a: The outline is fixed before any number is computed: a named park polygon from OpenStreetMap, or the client’s own drawing. For works not yet started, the outline, the baseline and the twelve comparison places are registered with a date and a hash. Six Brussels projects are registered that way today.

faq.q: How often is the detector wrong?
faq.a: Checked against an independent map made from aerial photographs, Groenkaart Vlaanderen 2018 against 2021 and 2024, in Antwerp and Ghent, with the same matched places and its own noise threshold. Where the aerial map sees no change beyond noise, the satellite agrees in {spec}. Where the satellite says the canopy changed beyond noise, the map agrees in only {agree}; the sharpest disagreements, checked on photographs, were lush meadows after the 2018 drought read as trees and a park’s pond refilled. So a change beyond noise is a candidate, not a proof: a loss is named only when a second instrument and documents agree.

faq.q: How is this different from the official Copernicus layers?
faq.a: Those layers say how much green and canopy a city has. Frondia says whether that changed beyond the city’s own noise, where, and, with documents, why. It sits on top of them.

faq.q: What about street trees and small squares?
faq.a: Below about a hectare the signal drowns: four planted streets inside a 19-hectare sector add roughly half a hectare of canopy, diluted forty times. For small things Frondia checks something else: whether the object appeared at points named in advance, with points that were not named as the comparison.

faq.q: Which cities, and can it move to another one?
faq.a: {cities}. The threshold belongs to the pair of city and instrument: {wider}. A new city gets its own calibration.
Summer composites from 2017 to 2026. Monitoring runs every season, {seasons} so far in every city, and each season gets its own threshold.

cases.title: Three measured cases instead of promises

what.ninove: wasteland by the canal → park, {ha} ha

cases.note: This is not a forecast for this sector but the range measured on comparable works: a change of cover over most of a site gives an effect more than twice the threshold, and it holds for years. The size depends on what was there before: wasteland gives more than a quayside that was already green.

left.lead: What this table leaves out on purpose.
left.body: Cooling: the significance threshold for surface temperature came out at 1.32 °C, more than the realistic effect of an urban park, so there are no claims about degrees here. The cost of an effect: prices compare only within one type of work, and the budgets of comparable projects are published only in part.

commitment.title: What exactly we will check, and when we will refuse

items.lead: The footprint of the works is fixed before they start.
items.body: The polygon, its hash and the date enter the register before the first day of works. Drawing it afterwards around whatever turned green becomes impossible.

items.lead: The control is named at the same time.
items.body: {controls} sectors that resemble the site in its state before the works, none closer than {km} km. The list is published before the measurement; if no comparable control exists, that is recorded as a refusal, not adjusted.

items.lead: The threshold comes from the city’s calibration,
items.body: not chosen for the result: the null distribution is computed with the same matching and the same images as the audit itself, the way the trend’s threshold above was.

items.lead: The comparison window is built from the completion date:
items.body: a baseline before the works begin, the assessment two years after they end. If the works fall inside a window, the audit declines to compute.
Greenness and land-cover classes from the same images: the first says that something changed, the second what exactly, down to “unsealed but not planted”.

items.lead: A refusal is a published outcome.
items.body: Fewer than {minScenes} images in a window, a gap to the control above {maxGap}, works outside the window: no verdict is given, and that is printed alongside the results.

limits.title: What the method will not measure, even when everything is done right
items: Cooling of air or surface: the channel’s noise is larger than a realistic effect.
Restoration of existing green: repairing paths and ponds does not change vegetation.
Scattered street planting measured at the level of a sector: half a hectare of new canopy on nineteen hectares is lost.
The cause of a change: the satellite names the place, documents name the cause. Without a document a change is published as a measurement, not as anyone’s credit.
Young plantings in their first years: saplings on a meadow read less green than the grass they replaced, and honest greening can measure as a loss.

colophon.v: The city package’s Article 8 layer (2024 levels and the trend against control), the city manifest (thresholds and where they come from), the audit cases, the register of named points, Statbel (sectors, population, income, the 2021 census). Imagery: Copernicus Sentinel-2 with the Cloud Score+ mask, Google Dynamic World V1.

Every number leads to a layer of the city package, and the limits are printed next to the numbers, not in a footnote. The evidence does not change with the wording: numbers, thresholds and controls are recomputed from those files.

method.label: Method
method.title: How it reads
rules: It never counts, estimates or ranks: every number on this site stays with the engine.
Every measure carries the words it rests on, and a quote counts only if it is found word for word in the contract’s page.

A contract commits when it plans, funds or carries out a measure that changes vegetation cover. Greening named only as an aim, a need or better access is an aim. A description of what exists, a diagnosis or a place name is no measure.
The prompt, the output schema and the model are fixed and hashed. A changed prompt is a new version with a new check.
The 30 test contracts were drawn by seed before any of them was read. The ten the prompt was written against are kept apart and never counted in the rate.
It ran through Claude Code on the author’s own account with tools, connectors and project files switched off: it saw the prompt and one contract’s text, nothing else.

list.label: The register
list.title: Ninety-eight contracts, in their own words
list.blank: The page gives no description: only photo credits and the budget.

limits.label: Limits
limits.title: What it does not tell you
items: “Commits” records a promise made in a contract. Whether the ground changed is the atlas’s question, and it can answer only where a footprint of about a hectare exists; most of these measures are streets, courtyards and squares below that.
The contracts publish no perimeter in a machine-readable form, so a measure cannot be placed on the map. Its place is the name the text gives.
It reads the summary on quartiers.brussels, not the programme documents. The pages of 41 contracts, all started between 1994 and 2006, carry no summary at all.
Beliris projects and the region’s own parks are not in this register.
limits.last: Thirty contracts give a wide interval, printed with every rate. The rate holds for this prompt and this model only.

communes.title: Communes the law counts in {city}

communes.source: The EEA and JRC method (NRR_Art8) repeated on open data: LAU 2024, degree of urbanisation 2024, urban centres and clusters 2021 (1 km² grid), CLCplus Backbone 2021 for green, the Woody Vegetation Layer 2021 for canopy. The 2021 layers are allowed for draft plans only.

communes.leaveOut: Leaving out all {n} would take {area} of the region’s area and {res} of its residents out of the count, but {woody} of its woody vegetation. The duty of no net loss would rest on {rest} dense communes, {restGreen} green on average.

unstable.water: {name} is {pts} points over the line. Without water counted as green, one of the other readings of Article 3(20) the test runs, it is {gnw}, and {name} would not be exempt: the verdict turns on that reading.

balance.title: Since the {base} base
balance.limit: Hectares as a satellite classifier reads them, not the official CLCplus and Woody Vegetation layers, which do not exist yet for 2025 and 2026. One summer against another is noisier than a four-year window. A park that loses trees can read as more built-up, when a mixed pixel changes class.
balance.lede: Summer {base} against summer {s}, in hectares as Dynamic World classifies the ground; urban green as the Regulation reads it, trees, grass, shrub and water, not farmland. A sector counts only where it moved beyond noise against its twelve matched places.
balance.raw: Without subtracting matched places, {city} would show {g} of green and {b} built-up between summer 2024 and summer {s}. The classes shift from one summer to the next; the matched places take that shift out.
balance.preliminary: Summer {y} has fewer than eight usable scenes: its figures are preliminary.
